newsitem.title: CHINA: China snows kill 10, strand nearly 1,000.
newsitem.headline: China snows kill 10, strand nearly 1,000.

text.p: The heaviest snows in 30 years have caused 10 deaths and stranded nearly 1,000 gold miners in a remote corner of China's westernmost Xinjiang region, officials said on Wednesday.

Another 29 people were missing after the snowfalls in the Altay region snapped telephone lines and made roads impassable, cutting off mountain villages, officials said by telephone from the town of Altay.
A local official said 10 people had frozen to death and another 10 were suffering from severe frostbite, while about 1,000 gold miners had been trapped in surrounding mountains by the snow.

Helicopters have been used to bring in relief supplies and hunt for the missing since the snowstorms began nearly two weeks ago, they said. Officials had allocated more than 25 million yuan (US$3.0 million) for disaster relief.
Officials estiamted about 186 homes have been damaged by the snow, which reached a height of 40 cm (16 inches) on average and 2.4 metres (yards) in some areas.
Medical teams were being organised for the worst-hit areas and People's Liberation Army soldiers were helping with relief work.

Many of the people in the sparsely-populated region are nomads who raise cattle, goats or sheep for a living. More than 50,000 head of livestock, mostly sheep, had died and another 580,000 were short of food.
The news agency also said that some 580,000 head of cattle and other livestock were now short of feed in the area.
